Rarely used cards (Always ignore, Prompt library, Workflow, Release report) are folded with an "Advanced" label; click the card title to open it, and searching to it opens it by itself.

how.t: Click the "Search settings" box under the Settings heading (or press /)

how: Use ↑ ↓ to choose then Enter, or click a result

title: See disk usage and clean up data on this machine
what: Shows how much the app takes on this machine (a bar split by part: Database, AI sessions, Downloaded tag photos, AI run history, Server log, Telegram sign-in, Configuration), the database by table and by group. Clear one part at a time: handled messages older than 30 days, Briefing summaries, the old send log, finished AI sessions, downloaded photos, AI run history, the server log, one group's data, reply drafts in this browser. Each clear asks first and says what is lost and what is kept; the database is compacted afterwards. On startup the app removes photos older than 30 days, AI runs older than 90 days and trims a log over 5 MB. The "Change folder" button (bottom of the Disk usage card, next to the path) moves all the data to another folder: type an absolute path, the app restarts, switches to the new place only once the move is done, then deletes the old copy; on failure it keeps using the old folder. If that folder already holds Radar data (a disk used with another install), the dialog asks "Use the data there": the app switches to that data and the data in use stays where it was, not deleted. Not available while the AI Agent is running; cloud-synced folders (iCloud, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) are refused because they corrupt the database. If the new folder is on an external disk, the disk must be plugged in when the app opens.
how: Look at the "Disk usage" card: the total, what can be cleared now, and the split by part

how.t: Click "Clear" on the tile to clean up; each tile shows its size, item count, since when, and whether it comes back
Read the confirmation; click "Cancel" to leave (only click "Clear" if you really want to)

title: Choose a role (Dev / QA/QC / PO/PM)
what: The role decides the home page, the Dashboard and the AI's point of view when summarizing and creating tickets; QA and PO don't use the AI Agent. Without a role, Telegram acts as Dev.
keys: role dev qa qc po pm clear role

title: Privacy: hide phone numbers / emails sent to AI
what: Other people's messages and ticket text are sent to the AI you choose. "Hide phone / email sent to AI" replaces phone numbers and emails with [phone] / [email] before sending (drafts, summaries, Briefing, Q&A, YouTrack AI). The "Show message text in macOS notifications" switch (off by default) is not here but in Settings › Telegram › "Notifications".
how: Open Settings › AI and scroll down to "Privacy"
Turn the switch on / off; it takes effect right away
keys: privacy hide phone email notification text redact

title: Open the app in a new browser (access code)
what: The dashboard's API only accepts browsers that have been granted access, so other programs on the machine (the AI Agent included) cannot send messages for you. Opening the app with Start Dashboard or the myradar open command grants the browser access automatically for about a year. If you see the lock screen: reopen the app one of those two ways, or paste the code from the file ~/.telegram_dashboard/api_token and click "Unlock".
how: Open the app with Start Dashboard / myradar open (or uv run python -m telegram_dashboard open)
On the "This browser is not unlocked yet" screen: paste the code and click "Unlock"
keys: access code token sign in lock open app bookmark browser unlock

title: Language (Match device / Tiếng Việt / English)
what: Choose the app's language; "Match device" uses Vietnamese when the device does, English otherwise. Also switchable with the VI / EN button on the top bar. Saved in the browser.
keys: language english vietnamese match device ngon ngu

title: Appearance, style, font, AI mascot, accent color, gradient
what: Choose Light / Dark / System; the Simple / Default / Vivid style; the font (Quicksand, Be Vietnam Pro, Inter, Nunito or the system font); the text size (Small / Medium / Large / Extra large); the AI mascot that replaces the robot in every loading scene, empty page and AI box (by default your role's creature: a white coder dragon for Dev, an owl with a magnifier for QA/QC, a fox showing the way for PO/PM; or the robot, an AI drawing from your description, your own image; it also replaces the AI Agent icon on buttons and menus); the accent color (a preset, the slider, or the eyedropper button for any color / hex code) and Strength; turn on Gradient with a second color or pick a Blend. The Preview beside it (Group chat / Ticket / Loading) recolors as you drag. Saved in the browser.

how.t: Open "Font" and pick the font you like

Under "AI mascot" pick the robot or a role's creature (none picked: your role's, following a change of role; once picked, it stays; they blink and wave like the robot), click the sparkle tile to have AI draw one from a description (tap an idea or type your own, pick the Cute / Pixel / Line art style, optionally add a "Reference picture" (pick a file or paste one) for the AI to draw after, change the drawing model / effort right in the box (by default the "Summaries, drafts" picks), preview it in the app, then click "Use this mascot" (the AI picks out the eyes and an arm so it blinks and waves like the robot; if it can't, the still one is used); the AI draws in the background, so you can close the window and carry on, and a notice with "View" tells you when it is done), or click the image tile to upload your own (a PNG / JPG / WebP on a one-colour or checkerboard background loses it; the picture wiggles hello when shown, breathes and tilts its head now and then)
Turn on "Gradient" to add a second color

keys: appearance theme light dark system style simple default vivid font text size accent color gradient
